answer: The ferrous multiplier is published, charged in trellis, and signal lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 12 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 1515 identities would post 1310 proofs and burn roughly 47 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
